transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-07-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Lina Park (Archer, Head of ML), Raj Patel (Archer, Platform), Sofia Morales (Archer, Security)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping to decide hosting mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private), success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan and timeline.

Topics:
- Current stack and constraints
- Success metrics (latency, cost per 1k tokens, availability)
- Data residency and compliance requirements
- Benchmarking plan and pass/fail criteria
- Pilot timeline and kickoff

Transcript:
00:00:03 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um quick intro — i'm Maya i'm the AE for the Archer account, and with me is Diego who'll lead the technical bits.
00:00:12 Diego Alvarez: Hey, hi all. I'll try to keep the deep stuff digestible, but please interrupt for clarifications.
00:00:20 Lina Park: Thanks. Quick background — we are building an assistant for operations and financial forecasting, so low-latency generation for short prompts and embeddings for search. We have some PII in the prompts so security is important.
00:00:38 Raj Patel: Our throughput is bursty — peak of about 120 rps for short queries but average around 20 rps, and we expect 2x growth in next quarter.
00:00:50 Sofia Morales: From security we need SOC 2, SSO, RBAC, KMS integration, and audit logs. Data residency in EU for certain customers is non-negotiable.
00:01:05 Maya Chen: Great — that gives us the constraints. So the goal today is to lay out what a 2–3 week POC looks like, what pass/fail looks like, and which hosting mode makes sense. Quick question: is there a hard timeline for go-live?
00:01:20 Lina Park: Ideally before end of Q3, so September rollout. POC needs to be done by mid-August to plan capacity.
00:01:29 Maya Chen: Ok, mid-August POC completion makes sense.
00:01:34 Diego Alvarez: On hosting options — brief recap: Hosted = quickest, no infra to run, Redwood manages keys and runtime; Dedicated = reserved GPU pool, predictable throughput and more isolation; Private = VPC or on-prem, customer-managed infra, max control. Tradeoffs are typical: latency/cost, data control, and operational burden.
00:02:01 Raj Patel: I want to call out cost predictability as top priority — we need predictable unit economics, otherwise finance won't sign off.
00:02:08 Maya Chen: Noted — we'll include cost per 1k tokens estimates for all modes. Diego, can you outline benchmark methodology?
00:02:16 Diego Alvarez: Sure. We'll run 3 benchmark buckets: cold-start latency, steady-state latency under our sequence length mix, and throughput scaling to peak rps. We'll use a small sample dataset you provide and a synthetic burst generator. Measured metrics: p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and cost estimate. We'll also surface token-level cost and failed request rate.
00:02:48 Lina Park: For success criteria, we want p95 < 450ms for 32-token prompts and p99 < 900ms, error rate < 0.5%, and < 25% increase over our current baseline for unit cost. Also data residency and KMS integration required for private/customer data flows.
00:03:10 Sofia Morales: Also audit logs retention for 90 days and SSO via SAML.
00:03:16 Maya Chen: Ok that's concrete. For POC modes — here's how we propose to run them: Hosted pilot first to validate functional correctness and quality, then Dedicated for throughput/latency economics, and if compliance blocks hosted/dedicated we'll pivot to Private. Does that sequence make sense?
00:03:34 Raj Patel: Sounds reasonable, so hosted first, dedicated second. Private is a fallback if compliance blocks us.
00:03:40 Diego Alvarez: For the hosted run we'll provision an isolated tenant with EU-backed instances and explicit KMS integration. We'll also enable prefix cache and batching suggestions to mirror your production traffic.
00:03:52 Lina Park: How do you ensure EU residency in hosted mode?
00:03:56 Diego Alvarez: We can pin the region to eu-west-1 and have the logs/audit retained in that region. KMS can be customer-managed keys in our hosted offering — there is a short setup.
00:04:07 Sofia Morales: We'll need an architecture diagram for that flow.
00:04:10 Maya Chen: We'll share a diagram after the call.
00:04:14 Diego Alvarez: For Dedicated, you get reserved GPU pool. We'll size nodes based on QPS and the model you pick. Quick math: if you run an LLaMA-variant 13B quantized with our inference profiles, you'll get roughly X tokens/sec per GPU depending on sequence length; we'll convert to nodes in the benchmark plan. We'll ask for representative sequences to compute sharper numbers.
00:04:40 Raj Patel: When you say 'X' tokens/sec can you get us numbers tuned to our payload? We can't work with placeholders.
00:04:45 Diego Alvarez: Yes — Diego: action item, i will run an initial estimate today with the dataset you share.
00:04:51 Maya Chen: We'll include that in the deliverables.
00:04:55 Lina Park: On timeline, can we do hosted pilot 7/27–8/09, then dedicated bench 8/10–8/20? That gives us mid-August results.
00:05:05 Maya Chen: That schedule aligns with our resources, yes — Diego confirm availability.
00:05:08 Diego Alvarez: I have capacity for those windows. We'll need the dataset and a short list of model variants you want to test by 7/23.
00:05:18 Raj Patel: OK we'll aim to send that by Friday 7/23 end of day.
00:05:23 Sofia Morales: Security docs — can you share SOC 2 and encryption/arch docs and the KMS setup guide?
00:05:30 Maya Chen: Yes, we'll send SOC 2 attestation, encryption guide, and an onboarding checklist.
00:05:36 Lina Park: For benchmarks, what about run-to-run variance — we need reproducible harness and seed control.
00:05:42 Diego Alvarez: We'll provide the harness as a reproducible repo and we'll pin random seeds where applicable. We'll run 3 runs and report median and stdev.
00:05:52 Raj Patel: If hosted doesn't meet p95 SLA, will Redwood allow fall-back to dedicated during POC?
00:05:58 Diego Alvarez: Yes, we can do an A/B fallback — our routing supports model variant fallback and routing to dedicated capacity if latency targets aren't hit, though dedicated provisioning takes lead time. For the POC we can provision dedicated temporary nodes for the bench.
00:06:12 Lina Park: What's the expected cost for a two-week dedicated bench run?
00:06:16 Maya Chen: We'll put an estimate in the comparison doc — depends on GPU type but ballpark will be in the deliverables.
00:06:22 Sofia Morales: Any competitors we should be aware of? We've seen pitches from Anthropic and CloudVendorX; also evaluating whether to keep inference in-house.
00:06:30 Maya Chen: noted
00:06:33 Diego Alvarez: Security note — if you need fully air-gapped on-prem we'll map out the on-prem private deployment but that is the longest lead time and higher engineering lift.
00:06:45 Lina Park: Understood.
00:06:48 Maya Chen: Great, let's recap next steps and owners.
00:06:53 Maya Chen: Recap: Maya to send hosting comparison, pricing and SOC2/encryption docs by 7/22. Diego to share benchmark harness repo and initial model token/sec estimates by 7/23. Archer to share dataset and traffic profile by 7/23. We'll target hosted pilot 7/27–8/09 and dedicated bench 8/10–8/20, with POC wrap-up mid-August.
00:07:20 Raj Patel: Sounds good.
00:07:23 Lina Park: One more question — do you support custom quantization profiles? We saw some notes in docs.
00:07:30 Diego Alvarez: Yes, we support per-model quantization profiles as part of the Optimize toolkit; we'll recommend quantization for dedicated to save cost while measuring quality regression.
00:07:41 Sofia Morales: For the KMS, any limit on key rotations and HSM support?
00:07:46 Maya Chen: We support customer-managed KMS with rotation policies; HSM depends on Private deployments but we can discuss.
00:07:55 Raj Patel: ok
00:07:58 Maya Chen: Any blockers from Archer side today?
00:08:02 Lina Park: No blockers; action items are clear. We'll get the dataset and traffic numbers.
00:08:07 Maya Chen: Perfect. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the pilot windows and a 30-minute kickoff for the hosted run.
00:08:14 Diego Alvarez: I'll start prepping the harness and run a quick estimate later today.
00:08:20 Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll send notes and deliverables.

[End of recording]
